title: Associated primes of a nonzero principal quotient of a normal Noetherian domain
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $a\in A$ be nonzero. An associated prime of $A/aA$ means a prime ideal equal to the annihilator $\{r\in A: r\bar c=0\}$ of some nonzero $\bar c\in A/aA$. Every such associated prime $\mathfrak p$ has height one: $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$, and there is no strict chain of prime ideals of length greater than one ending at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: For every prime q, Mathlib gives that A_q is a domain and is integrally closed. Apply the forward implication of Serre criterion normal and retain its S2 conclusion.

Since A is a domain and a is nonzero, a is a nonzerodivisor. Apply the existing S2 regular quotient associated-height theorem to obtain height(p) at most one. This packages the localization and depth argument of the original steps 3 through 6.

The element a annihilates every quotient element: lift it to b in A and observe that ab belongs to the principal ideal (a). Association implies containment of the module annihilator in p, hence a belongs to p. As a is nonzero, p is not the zero ideal. Mathlib height_eq_zero_iff_eq_bot for domains gives height(p) nonzero, hence at least one. Antisymmetry with the upper bound gives height(p)=1.
